newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FULL TEXT-Burns Philp herb/spice sale.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-Burns Philp herb/spice sale.

text.p: Yeast and spice group Burns Philp & Co Ltd announced on Monday it would sell its U.S. and European spice and herb businesses so it could focus on its yeast business and that its managing director Ian Clack would retire.
It also announced third quarter profits and previewed fourth quarter profits.
A full text of that announcement follows.
1. Intention to sell herb and spice businesses

Burns Philp has conducted a comprehensive review of all its operations in conjunction with The Boston Consulting Group including an assessment of the amount of time and resources required to generate adequate returns from its herb and spice businesses and the growth opportunities available to the company in yeast and related products.

Burns Philp intends to sell its consumer spice and industrial food service operations in North America and Europe to focus on the company's global yeast business. No changes are planned for the company's Investments division.
2. Board and management changes

Mr Ian Clack has informed the board of his intention to retire. The board has asked Mr Clack to stay on in an interim capacity while a search is conducted for a suitably qualified replacement, and he has agreed to this.
An international executive search firm will be appointed as soon as possible to conduct the search.
Mr John Cowling has announced his retirement from the board and the company.
Mr Geoff Schaeffer takes on Mr Cowling's responsibilities for the Yeast/Bakery division in addition to his responsibility for the company's investments division.

Together with the recent resignation from the board of the late Mr Andrew Turnbull, these changes will significantly alter the composition of the board. The current Chairman, Mr Alan McGregor has previously indicated his wish that be not be Chairman on a long term basis.
The search for a new Chairman and external directors is underway.
3. Q3 and Year to Date Result

* Lower than anticipated herb and spice sales in North America and production problems, at the Ankeny facility contributed to a A$24.4 million loss after tax for the group for the third quarter of the 1996-97 financial year.

* This loss was struck on revenue of $453 million and reflects an EBIT loss of A$10.5 million. After adjusting for businesses sold in 1996 this represents a revenue increase of 2 percent and a trading NPAT decline of $25.8 million.
* For the year-to-date revenues were $1,493 million, generating EBIT of A$78.2 million, and a net profit after tax and before abnormal items of A$26.6 million.

* The businesses to be sold (North American and European spice) recorded an EBIT loss of A$31.7 million for the year to date, whereas the businesses to be retained generated EBIT of A$106.1 million, marginally below last year to date.

* Our current expectations for the fourth quarter of the 1996/97 financial year are that the businesses to be sold will improve on the third quarter position, but still fall short of the result achieved in the fourth quarter of 1995/96.
* The Board will review the carrying value of all assets in light of these decisions and the status of discussions with interested parties prior to finalising the year end accounts.
This exercise may involve some write- offs or value adjustments.
4. Businesses to be sold
Barings have been given the mandate to sell:
- The businesses making up Burns Philp's herb and spice businesses in North America and Europe.
- The businesses intended for sale include: Durkee-French, Spice Islands, Tone's, British Pepper & Spice, Euroma and Ostmann
- The businesses may be sold separately on a geographic basis or together to one buyer.
- A number of the world's largest food companies have previously expressed interest in acquiring some or all of these businesses.
- It is expected the sale process may take up to six months.
5. Focus on Yeast

Burns Philp will use the funds released from the sale to reduce debt and focus on expanding the company's global businesses in yeast and related products, to take advantage of some current opportunities.

These businesses had 1996 sales of $1.2 billion and contributed the majority of the group's profits. Burns Philp is the world's largest manufacturer of fresh bakers yeast with 36 plants in 21 countries.

It is proposed that the ongoing business will manufacture and market bakers yeast and specialty yeasts, yeast extracts, consumer yeast,vinegar, and ingredients closely aligned with the bakery trade in Australasia, Europe, South and North America and Asia.
6. Chairman comment
Burns Philp's Chairman, Mr Alan McGregor, said that the decision to sell the spice business had been difficult.

"The board believes that this decision is in the best interests of all our shareholders. Focussing our resources on what is already a successful yeast business will provide a solid base for providing acceptable returns and growth to our shareholders".
"At the same time the spice businesses will be attractive to companies which have a substantial presence in the consumer products industry."
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
